facts.text: The far-left and far-right historic entrance doors have automatic push-plate controls. Wheelchairs and ECVs can be rented at the box office, first come, first served.
quote: Our historic front doors are heavy. Doors to the far left and far right have push-plates mounted on the wall for automatic opening.
Wheelchairs and ECVs are available for rental on a first-come, first-served basis from the box office.

facts.text: Universal restrooms on Mezzanine B and the lower level near Westheimer Gallery have adult changing tables.
facts.quote: There are adult changing tables located in the Universal Restrooms on the Mezzanine B level and on the Lower level, near the entrance to the Westheimer Gallery.

facts.text: The visitor page links to accessibility and sensory maps.
Visitors may bring food and drinks for seated dining areas; these are prohibited in museums, exhibitions and the OMNIMAX theater.
facts.quote: Guests are permitted to bring their own food and drinks into the building for consumption in seated dining areas. For the safety and preservation of our exhibits and artifacts, food and drink are not permitted to in museums, exhibits or The Robert D. Lindner Family OMNIMAX ® Theater.

facts.text: Medication, pumped milk and required food that must stay cold can be kept in the refrigerator in the Public Safety Quiet Zone.
facts.quote: Medication, pumped milk and required food items that need to stay chilled can be stored in the refrigerator in the Public Safety Quiet Zone as needed.

facts.text: The accessibility page lists adult changing tables (up to 400 lb) in universal restrooms on the Concourse, on the Mezzanine and on the Lower Level near the Museum of Natural History & Science.
facts.quote: Adult changing tables (holding up to 400 lb.) are located in universal restrooms in the Concourse, on the Mezzanine and on the Lower Level near the Museum of Natural History & Science.

facts.text: OMNIMAX wheelchair seating is at the top of the dome, and staff will help guests up the elevator.
facts.quote: Accessible, wheelchair seating is offered at the top of the OMNIMAX ® dome. OMINMAX ® staff are happy to assist guests up the elevator.

facts.text: OMNIMAX films offer audio description, closed captioning and assistive listening on request.
facts.quote: films offer descriptive audio, closed captioning and assisting listening. Tools are available upon request.

facts.text: The museum suggests weekday afternoons from 3 to 5 p.m. as the quietest time. From December 2026 a short pipe-organ performance (about 3 minutes) is planned on Sunday afternoons at 4:15 p.m.
quote: If you are looking for the quietest time to explore, join us weekday afternoons from 3 to 5 p.m.
Starting in December 2026, we will be adding a short, 3-minute pipe organ performance on Sunday afternoons at 4:15 p.m.

facts.text: Deaf Days with ASL are held at least once during each featured exhibit, and a script of featured-exhibit audio is available at the box office.
quote: Script version of featured exhibit audio is available upon request (see box office) Deaf Days are held at least once per the run of a Featured Exhibit
Join us for ASL interpreted tours! Interpreters from Cincinnati State’s Interpreter Training Program (ITP) will be partnering with Cincinnati Museum Center for ASL interpreted tours.

facts.text: The museum says it does not provide social stories, visual schedules or first/then boards.
facts.quote: Given the size of Union Terminal and “choose your own adventure” style of exploration, we do not provide social stories, visual schedules, or first/then boards.

facts.text: A caregiver visiting to support a person with a disability can receive a free Museum Admission ticket at the box office. The museum says caregivers still pay for OMNIMAX and featured exhibits.
facts.quote: Caregivers, who are visiting the museum for the purpose of providing care to an Individual with Disabilities, will be able to receive a free, complementary Museum Admission ticket. The caregiver will need to visit the box office to receive their ticket. As a reminder, the caregiver comp ticket only applies to the Museum Admission ticket. Caregivers will need to pay to visit OMNIMAX ® and Featured Exhibits.

facts.text: Mobility-equipment rentals are cashless. Renters must be over 18 and sign a rental agreement; the box office holds a driver’s licence or credit card until the wheelchair or ECV is returned.
quote: Renters must be over 18 years old and sign the Guest Mobility Equipment Rental Agreement. A driver’s license or credit card will be held at the box office until the wheelchair or ECV is returned.
All mobility equipment rentals are cashless.

facts.text: The museum links photo walkthroughs under “Accessibility Amenities” for preparing a visit, including guides to quiet zones, restrooms and individual museums.
quote: However, feel free to check out our museum focused “Accessibility Amenities” guides on the top right of this page listed under “Additional Information” to build your own or has a visual walkthrough of our galleries before visiting.

Accessibility Amenities in Museum of Natural History & Science Accessibility Amenities in Cincinnati History Museum Accessibility Amenities in The Children’s Museum OMNIMAX ® and Featured Exhibits Accessibility Amenities Food, Beverage and Additional Accessibility Amenities Quiet Zones & Restrooms Accessibility Amenities

facts.text: The museum lists 20 parking spaces for vehicles with registered disability decals, first come, first served. For help entering the building, call Public Safety at 513-287-7048 at least 24 hours ahead to arrange assistance.
facts.quote: For guests with officially registered disability decals, 20 parking spaces are designated and available on a first-come, first-served basis. For special assistance getting into the building, call Public Safety at (513) 287-7048 at least 24 hours in advance. An officer will arrange assistance for you.

facts.text: On entering the front doors, the Express Elevator is to the right and serves the lower level. The East Elevator is to the left and serves Mezzanine A, Mezzanine B and the lower level.
facts.quote: The Express Elevator, to the right of the main entrance as you come in the front doors, serves the Lower level (The Children’s Museum, restrooms, grab-and-go food service, Bean Sprouts and the Westheimer Gallery.) The East Elevator, to the left of the main entrance as you come in the front doors, serves the Mezzanine A level (Ruthven Gallery, Mallory Gallery, classrooms), the Mezzanine B level (Fountain Gallery, classrooms, restrooms) and the Lower level.

facts.text: An elevator just before the restrooms on the south side of the Rotunda goes to the mezzanine for the Holocaust & Humanity Center and Cincinnati History Library & Archives.
facts.quote: There is an elevator located just before the restrooms on the south side of the Rotunda that takes guests down to the Mezzanine level to access The Nancy & David Wolf Holocaust & Humanity Cetner and the Cincinnati History Library & Archives.

facts.text: An elevator just past the OMNIMAX entrance goes to the second floor north for visitors who cannot use the theater stairs.
facts.quote: There is also an elevator just past The Robert D. Lindner Family OMNIMAX ® Theater entrance. This elevator takes guests to 2nd floor north to enter/exit the OMNIMAX ® Theater if they cannot use the stairs.

facts.text: The museum describes the Public Safety quiet zone in the Rotunda as a shared space. It lists private nursing rooms by Fountain Gallery on the mezzanine and on The Avenue on the lower level.
quote: Nursing Room by Fountain Gallery (Mezzanine – Private Room)
Nursing Room on The Avenue (Lower Level – Private Room)

facts.text: Return equipment borrowed from a quiet zone to its original location or any ticket booth before leaving; the museum says visitors can keep used fidgets.
facts.quote: If you borrow equipment from a Quiet Zone during your trip, thanks for returning it to its original location or any ticketing booth before you leave. Used fidgets are yours to keep!

facts.text: The accessibility page describes manual-flush toilets and paper-towel dispensers in restrooms and notes that a few also have air hand dryers.
facts.quote: Manual flush toilets and paper towel dispensers. A few restrooms do have air hand dryers.

facts.text: The visitor page gives two ECV rental prices: $27 under Stroller & Mobility Rentals and $29 under Wheelchair & Electric Convenience Vehicle Rental. Confirm the current charge with the box office.
quote: Stroller & Mobility Rentals Strollers are available for rental on a first-come, first-served basis from the box office. Single strollers are $9 and double strollers are $11. Renters must be over 18 years old and sign the Guest Mobility Equipment Rental Agreement. A driver’s license or credit card will be held at the box office until the stroller is returned. Wheelchairs and ECVs are available for rental on a first-come, first-served basis from the box office. Wheelchairs are $7. ECVs are $27.

Wheelchair & Electric Convenience Vehicle (ECV) Rental Wheelchairs and Electronic Convenience Vehicles (ECVs) are available for rental on a first-come, first-served basis from the box office. Wheelchairs are $7. ECVs are $29.

facts.text: The museum lists 10 a.m.–2 p.m. hours on November 25 and December 24, 2026, and says it is closed on Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day. Its usual daily hours are 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
quote: Open daily: 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day Open from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on November 6, November 25 and December 24, 2026
